phase3_findings.description: Only the JsonBoundsError arm of _bounded_request_metadata returns discarded=True; the meta-read-error, non-dict meta, key-iteration-error and unexpected-exception arms also drop the whole _meta but return ({}, False), so the refusal line reads kept _meta keys=[] as if the caller sent nothing.

RuleSetRequestError.refusal_class strips the 'Request refused: ' prefix by convention; a message lacking it becomes the whole class, and the passed-checks rule for identity fields lives only at raise sites. _refusal_kind in safety/rule_sets.py repeats the prefix parsing.

audit_line outcome is a free-form str and identity travels as dict[str, Any] splatted into audit_line(**identity); a misspelled key would raise TypeError inside the finally block and replace the call's result or exception.

metadata_discarded is a separate bool next to metadata, so a non-empty metadata with metadata_discarded=True is representable and refusal_log_fields would name no keys; the only producer keeps them consistent today.
RefusalRedactingRunner's branch for an UnsafeSqlError or RlsError no guard logged first now logs class and kept-key fields, but no test asserts them.
test_no_rule_set_file_writes_no_audit_or_refusal_line only checks no message contains 'rule-set', so a differently worded new refusal line on the no-rule-set path would pass.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (six Suggestions and one inconclusive checklist item, nothing at or above the Important threshold)
The PR is ready to merge: every checklist claim that could be checked passed, all six acceptance criteria are covered, and no reviewer raised a finding at or above the Important threshold.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and an INCONCLUSIVE checklist item → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (6)

<details><summary>6 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/server.py` lines 315–341: only the `JsonBoundsError` arm of `_bounded_request_metadata` returns `discarded=True`. The arms for a `request_context.meta` read error, a non-dict `meta`, a key-iteration error and an unexpected bounding exception also drop the whole `_meta` but return `({}, False)`. The later refusal line then shows `kept _meta keys=[]`, which reads as if the caller sent nothing. The earlier server warning still records the drop. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 347–368: `RuleSetRequestError.refusal_class` is computed by stripping the `Request refused: ` prefix from the message, so a message without that prefix silently becomes the whole class. The rule that `rule_set`, `account_id` and `user_id` hold only values that passed their checks is enforced only at each raise site in `select_rule_set`. `_refusal_kind` in `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 717–725 recovers a guard refusal's kind with the same prefix-stripping approach. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 658–689: `audit_line(outcome: str, ...)` accepts any text, while only `served`, `refused: <class>` and `failed` are valid. The identity values travel in an untyped `dict[str, Any]` splatted into `audit_line(**identity)`, so a misspelled key would raise a `TypeError` inside the `finally` block and replace the call's own result or exception. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/server.py` (`_bounded_request_metadata`) and `query_database_impl_with_widgets`: `metadata_discarded` is a separate bool next to `metadata`, so the signature accepts a non-empty `metadata` together with `metadata_discarded=True`, in which case `refusal_log_fields` names no keys. The only producer keeps the two consistent today. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 791–799: the `RefusalRedactingRunner` branch for an `UnsafeSqlError` or `RlsError` that no guard logged first now writes `guard refused a statement: %s; <fields>`, but no test asserts its class and kept-key fields. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `tests/unit/test_rule_set_request_logging.py` lines 255–263: `test_no_rule_set_file_writes_no_audit_or_refusal_line` only checks that no log message contains the substring `rule-set`, so a new refusal line worded differently on the no-rule-set path would pass it. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred
- VC-15: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — Rule-set queries run with HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES removed from session sql_mode; CAST(x AS REAL) is sent as CAST(x AS FLOAT); PARTITION lists and index hints refused. [docs/external/rule-sets.md]

  Verified: sql_mode removal. factory.py:67 defines RULE_SET_REMOVED_SQL_MODES={HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE,NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES}, passed as remove_sql_modes when rule_sets is not None (factory.py:116); mysql/sql_runner.py:129-139 reads @@SESSION.sql_mode, filters those flags and runs SET SESSION sql_mode. PARTITION/index-hint refusal: safety/rule_sets.py:84,225 raise RuleSetRefusal(KIND_TABLE_OPTIONS) for table option args. Not verified: the CAST(x AS REAL) -> CAST(x AS FLOAT) claim. It depends on sqlglot's MySQL generator type mapping; no dependency_sources were supplied, no sqlglot source exists in the views (Glob for sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py found none), and the repo has no test or code asserting the REAL to FLOAT output (grep 'AS REAL' only hits the doc line). rule_sets.py:580 regenerates SQL with dialect mysql, so the mapping would apply, but I could not read it. Missing evidence: sqlglot dialects/mysql.py and generator.py TYPE_MAPPING, or running sqlglot.transpile('SELECT CAST(x AS REAL)', read='mysql', write='mysql').

  </details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A request whose `_meta` has more than 64 keys is refused as rule-set key missing, and its WARNING log line says SQL Lens discarded the request metadata for exceeding its limits and names no keys.
- [ ] Every refusal under a rule-set file is logged at WARNING once, with its refusal class and the names, never the values, of the `_meta` keys SQL Lens kept from the request; a guard refusal's class and key names are on the line #374 writes for it.
- [ ] Every rule-set request that `query_database` receives, whatever its ending, writes exactly one INFO audit line, counted over the log records captured for that one `query_database` call. The line names the outcome (served, the pre-agent refusal class, or failed for any other ending, a turn that ends on a guard refusal and a cancelled call included) and those of the rule set, account ID and user ID that passed their checks: a served request's line names all three, and a request refused as user ID invalid names the rule set and account ID but no user ID value.
- [ ] With no rule-set file configured, `query_database` writes no audit line and no refusal log line that it does not write today, and `[agent.audit]` stays unwired. A `query_database` call that the MCP SDK rejects for malformed arguments before `query_database` runs writes no audit line.
- [ ] A new external doc, `docs/external/rule-sets.md`, is the canonical definition of the version-1 rule-set format as SQL Lens loads it: every record, field, type, ID and identifier rule #374 states. It also states: - the config key, MySQL only, and restart to reload; - the five request classes and the `_meta` matching rules; - what the guard refuses, how it rewrites listed tables, and that a column outside the set fails as an unknown column; - the catalog rewrite and its 25 kept fields; - these limits: memory is shared by every rule set, so table and column names, SQL literal values, notes and chart data in curated memory can reach any role; the admin tools act for every rule set and belong only where end users' assistants cannot call them; `show_details` returns the SQL the model wrote, before the guard's rewrite; conversations are bound to identity; `verify-memory` is unsupported; SQL Lens trusts `_meta`, so any caller that can reach `query_database` chooses its rule set; `agent.standing_instructions` is shared by every rule set; a calling application that drops its own `_meta` keys looks like one that sent none; rule-set queries run with `HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE` and `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` off, and `||`, double-quoted text and backslashes in the model's SQL are read as MySQL's default `sql_mode` reads them (`OR`, strings and escapes), whatever the server's mode; `PARTITION` lists and index hints are refused and optimizer hints are dropped; `CAST(x AS REAL)` loses precision; a query without `ORDER BY` can return rows in the order of an index on a hidden column; an unqualified name the set hides can resolve to a same-named column of another table in the query; and syntax sqlglot writes back in a form MySQL rejects fails, or is refused when sqlglot cannot write it for MySQL. - It uses synthetic names only.
- [ ] `docs/external/row-level-security.md`'s "Rules filter rows, not columns" limit and `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md`'s "there is no table allow/deny-list" sentence point to rule sets for table and column limits on MySQL. `docs/external/configuration.md` documents the new config key and says in its `[agent.audit]` section that the rule-set audit line is written whatever `enabled` says, `docs/external/index.md` links the new doc, and `docs/internal/setup/preflight.md` states that the database probe runs the existence check when a rule-set file is configured.
